subject: Medicine
concept: Bone marrow aspiration and core biopsy directly evaluate hematopoiesis, marrow cellularity, architecture and infiltrative or neoplastic disease.

content.definition: Bone marrow aspiration and core biopsy directly evaluate hematopoiesis, marrow cellularity, architecture and infiltrative or neoplastic disease.
content.explanation: Aspiration samples liquid marrow for cellular morphology and ancillary studies; core biopsy preserves architecture and evaluates cellularity, fibrosis and infiltration.
content.mechanism: Aspiration samples liquid marrow for cellular morphology and ancillary studies; core biopsy preserves architecture and evaluates cellularity, fibrosis and infiltration.
content.clinical_relevance: Aspiration is useful for cellular morphology and many ancillary tests. Core biopsy evaluates architecture and fibrosis. A dry tap can occur with fibrosis or dense infiltration.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis uses the appropriate clinical, laboratory, microbiologic, marrow or blood-bank studies for the suspected condition.
content.treatment: Management is disease- and patient-specific and should follow current authoritative guidance.
